tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Thanks for being involved in this research. I'd like to ask you some questions about learning new hobbies. First, what kinds of hobbies do your friends or family have? Why do you think they enjoy doing them?
tasks.sample: My mom loves gardening, and my best friend is really into photography. I think they enjoy these hobbies for different reasons. For my mom, gardening is therapeutic. She says digging in the soil and watching things grow helps her forget about work stress. It's slow, peaceful, and rewarding. As for my friend, photography lets him capture moments and see beauty in ordinary things. He enjoys the creative side, choosing angles, playing with light. Both hobbies give them a sense of accomplishment, but in very different ways. One is about growing things, the other about capturing them. Either way, they both genuinely enjoy what they do.
tasks.analysis: 中文：感谢你参与这项研究。我想问你一些关于学习新爱好的问题。首先，你的朋友或家人都有哪些爱好？你认为他们为什么喜欢做这些事情？
tasks.title: Interview

tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Thanks for that. Now if your school or workplace were to organize after-work hobby clubs, which clubs do you think would interest the most people?
tasks.sample: I think a cooking club would attract the most people. Here's why. First, everyone eats, so cooking is a useful skill that applies to daily life. You're not just learning a random hobby, you're saving money and eating healthier. Second, cooking can be very social. People can bring their own dishes, share recipes, and even turn it into a friendly competition. Also, it's flexible. Beginners can learn basic knife skills, while more experienced cooks can try international cuisines. Compared to something like pottery or knitting, cooking has a much lower barrier to entry. You probably already have a kitchen at home. So yeah, cooking club would be a hit.
tasks.analysis: 中文：谢谢你的回答。现在，如果你的学校或工作场所要组织课后或下班后的爱好俱乐部，你认为哪些俱乐部会最吸引大多数人？
tasks.title: Interview

tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Great, that's helpful. Next, do you think hobbies should mostly be relaxing or is it better if they challenge you, why?
tasks.sample: Honestly, I think the best hobbies have both, relaxation and challenge. But if I had to pick one, I'd say a little bit of challenge is better in the long run. Purely relaxing hobbies like watching TV are fine, but they don't help you grow. A challenging hobby keeps your brain active and gives you a sense of progress. For example, learning to play the guitar is frustrating at first, but when you finally nail a song, that feeling is amazing. That said, hobbies shouldn't feel like a second job. They need to be enjoyable. So I'd say aim for something that pushes you a bit, but not to the point where you dread doing it.
tasks.analysis: 中文：很好，这很有帮助。接下来，你认为爱好应该主要以放松为主，还是最好能给你带来挑战？为什么？
tasks.title: Interview

tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Got it. Now. Last question. How important do you think it is for people to keep exploring new hobbies as they grow older, why?
tasks.sample: I think it's very important, maybe even more important than when you're young. Here's why. As people get older, their routines tend to shrink, same job, same social circle, same daily schedule. Exploring new hobbies brings fresh energy and prevents life from feeling stale. It also keeps the brain sharp. Learning something new, like a language or an instrument, builds new neural connections. That's good for mental health at any age. Plus, hobbies can introduce older adults to new communities. You might join a book club or a hiking group and make friends you wouldn't have met otherwise. So yeah, staying curious is a form of staying young. Hobbies help with that.
tasks.analysis: 中文：明白了。现在，最后一个问题。你认为随着人们年龄的增长，继续探索新的爱好有多重要？为什么？
tasks.title: Interview
